Two to five (2-5) years post-PhD research experience collecting, processing and analyzing geotechnical and/or geospatial data.
Master's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training (Preferred)
PhD in geotechnical engineering or geosciences or engineering (Preferred)

Minimum of three (3) years of professional or research experience collecting, processing and analyzing geotechnical and/or geospatial data, preferably within a university research, government, or non-profit environment.
Demonstrated experience leading and coordinating field teams in complex and challenging environments.
Demonstrated experience with project management and data management practices.
Experience working with or in the hazards community (e.g., emergency management, geoscience, climate resilience).
Experience with field work for geotechnical characterization under difficult conditions.
Demonstrated experience with field data analysis. Demonstrated experience with design and implementation of computational tools such as AI, machine vision, remote sensing data analysis.
Demonstrated experience with geospatial data analysis, field geodetic data collection (i.e. LiDAR, UAS, GPS, TLS).
Demonstrated experience with cyberinfrastructure development lifecycle for processing and managing complex, high-volume geospatial data with open-data principles.

The Research Associate is responsible for managing Geotechnical Extreme Event Reconnaissance Association (GEER) communications, operations, deployments, education and outreach and data archiving activities. This position coordinates the engagement of stakeholders in critical areas even before the occurrence of an event, manages virtual communications during reconnaissance, and facilitates collaborations with NHERI DesignSafe, NHERI Rapid and other partners. The Research Associate supports coordination with the science advisory groups (SAGs), virtual reconnaissance teams, and field deployment teams to ensure efficient data collection, indexing and communication of findings to advance hazard science. Additionally, this position assists with hosting virtual and in-person GEER events, outputs, communications and training.
Extreme Event Response - 30%

Support GEERs response during and after the extreme events that include; Earthquakes, Landslides & Ground Failures, Hurricanes & Typhoons, Floods & Extreme Storms, Wildfires, etc. Provide administrative and technical support using established procedures during the response (virtual and in-person) with an emphasis on ensuring that perishable data is made available through GEER and GEER partners.
Data Generation and Dissemination - 30%

Support GEER in the generation and dissemination of open AI-ready datasets that can be used to advance natural hazard research and science. Key part of this position is to strengthen the output of GEER so that extreme event reconnaissance data is readily available to the scientific community. Assist the reconnaissance team in creating such datasets as necessary.
Outreach and Communication Strategy - 30%

Lead the outreach and communication strategy of GEER with a focus on engaging the scientific community, engaging with GEER stakeholders, and communicating GEER findings. This includes operating the website, the newsletter and supporting the organization of GEER events to communicate the impact of GEER.
Data Management Protocols - 5%
Assists in developing protocols for data management and curation activities with a focus on AI-ready datasets. This includes protocols for data collection and data archiving in NHERI Designsafe.
Field Equipment and Deployment - 5%

Maintain field equipment and deploy as part of a GEER extreme events response team to areas affected by extreme events. Receive training and potentially deploy to disasteraffected areas with specialty equipment. Participate in reconnaissance studies and assist with data collection, particularly using equipment for which training will be provided.

Technical background to one of the following areas: field data acquisition, sensing (sensors, remote sensing), geospatial data analysis of optical, multi-spectral and radar imagery, or disaster data analysis using programming and AI.
Ability to foster collaborative relationships and provide essential support to research teams.
Excellent writing and oral communication skills.
